title: Best Three Score Average
statement:
Given score records, find the student whose best three scores have the largest average.

Contract
- `records` is non-null. Each record has a non-null student name and an integer score.
- Only the three highest scores for each student are considered. Students with fewer than three records are ignored.
- Return the name with the largest top-three total. Break ties by the lexicographically smallest name.
- Return the empty string when no student has three scores. Do not mutate `records`.

Examples
- `bestThreeAverage([Ada:90, Ada:95, Ada:100, Bob:100, Bob:70, Bob:60])` returns `Ada`.
- `bestThreeAverage([Nia:50, Nia:80, Omar:90])` returns the empty string.
- `bestThreeAverage([Amy:90, Amy:80, Amy:70, Bea:85, Bea:80, Bea:75])` returns `Amy`.

examples.input: records = [Ada:90, Ada:95, Ada:100, Bob:100, Bob:70, Bob:60]
records = [Amy:90, Amy:80, Amy:70, Bea:85, Bea:80, Bea:75]

hints: Group the scores by student before making comparisons.
A min-heap capped at size three keeps just one student's best three scores.
Compare sums rather than averages because every eligible student has exactly three kept scores. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(s) space for s students.
inputSyntax: Input: comma-separated name:score records, for example: Ada:90,Ada:95,Ada:100,Bob:100,Bob:70,Bob:60
